# Lakkhaṇamigajātaka (Ja 11)

**ID:** Ja 11
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Lakkhaṇamigajātaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The Lucky Deer
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja11

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Lakkhaṇamigajātaka* (Ja 11), translated by Bhikkhu Sujato as *The Lucky Deer* and known in E. B. Cowell's translation as the tale of "Luckie and Blackie", is a narrative of the Bodhisatta's past life set at the Bamboo Grove near Rājagaha concerning Devadatta [Braarvig; SuttaCentral]. In this past birth, the Bodhisatta was a chief stag who instructed his two sons in the art of herd leadership; one son (identified with Sāriputta) adhered to his father's advice and successfully led his herd to safety and prosperity, while the other son (identified with Devadatta) rejected his counsel and brought his herd to ruin [Nyanaponika et al. 2003]. The narrative exemplifies a regular pattern across the Jātaka collection illustrating the moral and practical dichotomies of wisdom versus foolishness and virtue versus wickedness in the past relationship between the Buddha's chief disciples and Devadatta [Braarvig].

Neither SuttaCentral nor the computational analyses of DharmaNexus record any Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language parallels for this text in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral documents six translations in four modern languages, including English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].
